evidence:
The workbook #21 requires a safe entrypoint, liveness gating, ordered suites, and reward on failure; frozen quality reference lines 92-94 and staged test.sh contract apply. Positive source evidence: task/tests/test.sh:60-61 writes the complete zero before app execution and installs cleanup; lines 68-83 refuse missing entry and unsupported/escaping symlinks; 104-113 launch UID/GID 65534 with env -i; 115-125 gate on HTTP; 193 exports the helper; 195-201 resolves context; 212-227 order gates, scorer, scored, scorer. There is no process-replacing shell exec. Task and frozen template test.sh have identical SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa, so these are shared-template defects, not unauthorized task drift.

Confirmed defects: (1) test.sh:154-159 only sends TERM and waits five seconds without requiring old-group death; 168-183 accepts any listener on port 3000 without proving the replacement owns it. In indexed original-term_ignored control, helper exited 0 after 5.707 s and logged new_pid=100 ready=1 despite EADDRINUSE; old PID 34 remained alive and the post-restart observation still contained volatile-marker. Original normal control replaced PID 8 with 24 and cleared memory, supplying the positive control. (2) cleanup at lines 33-39 executes unbounded wait before ensure_reward. The exact extracted original cleanup with its direct TERM-ignoring Node child exceeded the 10 s control deadline and needed external killing; child remained alive. A zero reward already existed, so this observation establishes a completion/safe-cleanup defect, not absence of all reward files. (3) after successful gates, lines 224-225 exit immediately on scored-suite error instead of invoking write_zero_reward. The original suite-tail controls simulated scored exit 124 and 2 using the actual unchanged scorer/policy: both retained reward=0, graded=1, no_op=0 and gates_passed=1. That contradicts staged contract item 8's plain zero on any scored failure and mislabels evaluator failure as grading. The gate-failure, successful 0.7 synthetic score, and malformed-score controls establish expected neighboring behavior; 0.7 is synthetic arithmetic, not an app judge score.

Additional bounded-liveness concern: test.sh:50 and :138 call urlopen(..., timeout=2).read() without an overall deadline. Current launcher-timeout-control executed that exact expression in the pinned verifier image and successfully read eight half-second chunks in 3.519 s. This proves timeout=2 is not a total read bound; indefinitely renewed chunks can stall the probe (inference, not a full-entrypoint hang run).

Evidence verification: recomputed all 181 unchanged_shared_harness_controls and all 6 current_launcher_socket_timeout_control artifact hashes against current raw-evidence-index.json; zero mismatches. Index SHA256 at review was a96ac601405a356d9565cb2f35aea3901673574c2225729f568c6a8180d9358a. results.json SHA256 is 602a0a7c49b5e8d91f00d3162624563ac46de941029d47754c73aaac58cec637; original-term_ignored/app-restart.log is 2bc2a2103b84affe79d5916d7b195dca778e0d561bc60927f3aa336e738666ce; original-scored_timeout/logs/reward.json is 0eb7ab1613764e6d861890a80946cf3b933b4a9d327156a1ce4f77e614bd44a5. Independently compared control fragments to current frozen bytes: helper-generation and cleanup functions match exactly; all six original suite tails match after only scorer-path relocation, and their scorer/policy files are byte-identical. Original-variant observations are used; proposed-patch passes do not clear this candidate. No new Docker/provider runs, task edits, configured judge run, Oracle or model-score claim.
counterexample: Broken alternative: a server that keeps snippets only in memory and installs process.on('SIGTERM',()=>{}) continues serving the same volatile records while the restart helper reports success, permitting false durability evidence; the exact helper control demonstrates this. Conforming alternative: a fully correct database-backed app passes gates but its scored evaluator exits 124 or 2; test.sh emits a graded zero despite evaluator failure, as the exact suite-tail controls demonstrate. A normally working server with a shutdown handler that never finishes also holds cleanup in wait despite the prewritten reward.
suggested_fix: Request a governed shared-template repair: ensure reward before bounded process-group cleanup, terminate and verify the old group before relaunch, verify the replacement listener, enforce a real readiness deadline, and write the canonical ungraded zero on scored-suite failure; preserve diagnostics and validate a newly frozen candidate without editing task-local harness policy to silence QC.
